I will keep my farm simple and steady this year. In Quzhou, the safest backbone for me is still the winter wheat and summer maize rotation, so I will put most of my land into that. I know this pattern, my equipment fits it, the buyers are easy to find, and it spreads labor across the year. Water matters here, so I will not chase crops that need more management or have a less certain market. I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed because I want stable emergence, stronger yield, and better resistance than old seed. On a small piece of land, I will plant peanuts to spread risk and bring in some cash if grain prices are weak.

For management, I will fertilize enough to protect yield but not overdo it because fertilizer is expensive and too much nitrogen can cause problems. For wheat, I will plough before sowing, apply base fertilizer, irrigate at the key stages, and do a couple of pesticide sprays only when I need to protect the stand from weeds, aphids, and disease. After wheat harvest, I will go straight into summer maize with no-tillage on that land so I can save time and hold moisture. I will topdress nitrogen for maize, irrigate when the crop is most sensitive, and keep pest control focused on the main problems instead of spraying too often. For peanuts, I will use lighter fertilizer with more phosphorus and potassium, keep the field clean, and manage moisture carefully because I do not want excess vegetative growth.
